findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The fan covers inside of the both walk in coolers of the meat/seafood department were observed with a significant amount of dust accumulation. Discussed with PIC. The facility plans to clean fan covers soon. Ensure that the fan covers of the walk in coolers are maintained and free of dust accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: A wet mop head was observed stored in the basin of the mop sink. Discussed with PIC and mop was repositioned. Ensure that wet mop heads are always stored in a manner that allows for them to properly air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed there to be no paper towels at one of the handwashing sinks in the seafood area. PIC noted that the handwashing sink barely gets used, as there is another one that is more accessible for employees to wash hands. Paper towels were provided at this hand sink. Ensure that there is always paper towels placed at each hand-sink in order to wash hands properly. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Several seafood items in a cooler were observed to be out of temperature. The surface temperatures ranged from 46-51F. The items were then probed and the readings were 45F (Cajun krab dip) and 51F(Salmon). PIC was unsure on how long the items were out of temperature. These items were placed on the first two rows on the middle and bottom shelves of the cooler. PIC observed the inspector taking temps and the items were pulled and discarded. Ensure that food items held in a cooler is always maintained at a temperature of 41F or less. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
A cooler was observed holding seafood items including but not limited to Salmon and seafood dips at improper temperatures. The surface temperatures ranged from 46-51F. The items were then probed and the readings were 45F (Cajun krab dip) and 51F(Salmon). PIC was unsure on how long the items were out of temperature. PIC observed the inspector taking temps and the items were pulled and discarded. Other items that were held at proper temperatures were kept. PIC noticed an accumulation of ice at the back of the bottom shelf of the cooler and mentioned that the facility will defrost and clean the cooler asap in order to remove the ice buildup. Ensure that cold holding equipment is maintained as frequent as necessary in order to provide sufficient temperatures for food items. 

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The knife holder was observed to contain an accumulation of dust and food debris.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure knife holder is cleaned regularly to prevent cross contamination.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The 3 part sink needs to be re-caulked.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure sink is caulked to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket at meat counter was observed at 0ppm quat. Solution was prepared earlier in the day and was discarded. Fresh solution at 150-200ppm was provided. Ensure quat solutions are changed as needed throughout daily operations and maintained at proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 A) Chlorinated cleaner connected to the wall mounted dispenser in the refrigerated meat room was observed to be clear in color, with approximately 1/4 of the product remaining. A new container of product that was yellow in color and unopened was observed under the 3 part sink. Product connected to dispenser was diluted and replaced with fresh chlorinated cleaner.
B) Sanitizer solution was not setup for use in the refrigerated meat room. Sanitizer was provided for use during inspection. Ensure sanitizer solutions are prepared and available for use when staff are working in the meat room.
Cleaning agents and sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Black wire shelving in meat department walk-in cooler was soiled with general buildup of debris, especially on lower shelves. Ensure wire shelving in the cooler is cleaned as needed.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 A) Handwashing sinks adjacent to 3 part sinks in Meat and Seafood Departments were soiled with grimy buildup. Sinks were cleaned during inspection. Ensure handwashing sinks are cleaned daily/as needed to eliminate general buildup.
B) Floor behind ovens in Seafood Department was soiled with what appeared to be food debris.
C) Floor in Meat Department walk-in cooler was soiled with meat splash and debris under shelving and along walls.
D) Fan covers of condensing units in refrigerated meat room were soiled with what appeared to be dust accumulation. 
Ensure cleaning occurs for the aforementioned items, and that physical facilities are maintained clean.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizer in the sani bucket in the meat area to be 0ppm of quat at the start of the inspection. Ensure sani bucket concentrations of quat are maintained between 200ppm and 400ppm. Additionally, solutions may need changed more frequently to ensure the proper concentration is maintained. Solutions were remade during the inspection. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Observed sanitizer in the 3 part sink and the sani bucket in the meat area to be 0-100ppm of quat at the start of the inspection. An employee was observed adding water to sanitizer solution when remaking the solution. Ensure extra water is not added to quat coming out of the dispenser. The dispenser is adjusted to dispense the proper concentration (200ppm-400ppm) of quat. Solutions were remade during the inspection. 
Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Observed the top oysters in the ice bath to be at a temperature of 50F-55F. The oysters were put on display a few hours ago from the cooler. A single layer of oysters was placed on the ice. The rest of the oysters were moved to the walk in cooler to get back down to 41 F. The manager stated she would find a better way to keep the oysters cold held properly. 
(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooking time and temperatures
findings.comment: Observed sani buckets to be sitting and used on the prep table. Ensure sani buckets are stored below the prep surface to prevent contamination of food being prepared. COS.
